query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Under dynamic loading, the dominant rate-controlling mechanism in solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is the enhanced activation of partial dislocations leading to twin formation at reduced stacking-fault energy. This mechanism confers increased strain hardening and elevated strength at lower temperatures and higher strain rates, while at higher temperatures and lower strain rates, dislocation slip dominates and lowers the strain-rate sensitivity.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, homogenized Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy with a solutionized single-phase FCC microstructure and minimal prior deformation.
generation.intervention: Systematically vary temperature (77–673 K) and strain rate (10−3 to 10^3 s−1) in both quasi-static (tensile) and dynamic (split-Hopkinson compression and tension) tests.
generation.conditions: Maintain consistent initial microstructure and loading geometry. Characterize deformation-induced features (dislocations, twins, shear bands) via EBSD and TEM after each test condition.
generation.structural_mediator: The fraction and distribution of twin boundaries and partial dislocations in the FCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: At lower temperatures and higher strain rates, partial dislocations become more active, forming twins that enhance strain hardening. This boosts dynamic strength and ductility. At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, recovery and cross-slip dominate, reducing the role of twinning and diminishing strain-rate sensitivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength and flow stress will show moderate to high rate sensitivity (e.g., increasing by ~50–100% from quasi-static to high strain rate), with greater twin boundary density observed at low temperatures and high strain rates. At elevated temperatures or slow strain rates, fewer twins form.
generation.baseline: Comparable or slightly higher dynamic strength and ductility than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi at similar loading conditions, based on reported performance in low-SFE high-/medium-entropy alloys.
generation.boundary: Temperatures from cryogenic to ~650 K and strain rates from 10−3 to 10^3 s−1. Outside this range, additional high-temperature processes (e.g., diffusion, phase transformations) may alter the mechanism.
generation.uncertainty: Exact strain-hardening increments and twin volume fractions remain unquantified for the full range of loading conditions without further data.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform split-Hopkinson compression tests at 77 K and 673 K, plus quasi-static and intermediate strain-rate tensile tests on identically processed FeNiCrMn. Quantify twin fractions and dislocation structures via EBSD/TEM after each test.
measurements: Yield strength and flow stress across strain rates (10−3 in tension to 10^3 s−1 in compression/tension).
Twinning incidence and dislocation density from microstructural characterization after deformation.
Hardening rate from stress–strain curves up to large plastic strains.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy does not exhibit increased twin density or strain hardening at high strain rates and low temperatures, or if the dynamic strength does not scale with the observed twin fraction, the proposed mechanism is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: These traits differ significantly from those that occur when quasi-static characteristics are present. The dynamic behavior of Al0.6CoCrFeNi biphasic (FCC and BCC) alloys was examined by Wang et al. []. The findings demonstrated that the yield strength could be clearly increased by increasing the strain rate. Tian et al. found that the AlCoCrFeNi alloy exhibited extremely high strain rate sensitivity by investigating the alloy at different strain rates []. The dynamic deformation mechanism of the CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy was investigated by Cao et al. []. It was found that massive dislocation nucleation and drag increased the strain rate sensitivity of the alloy at high strain rates, and the alloy also exhibited significant strain-hardening capability. Yuan et al. prepared Ni32Co30Cr10Fe10Al18 EHEAs by laser metal deposition, and it was found that the presence of the FCC phase caused the alloy to exhibit high ductility and strain-hardening ability at high temperatures and high strain rates []. Jeong Min Park et al. [] found that the CoCrFeMnNi alloy showed strong strain rate sensitivity. Compression experiments on the AlCrCuFeNi2 alloy at a strain rate of 10−3 s−1~3000 s−1 were

Park et al. [] had even found that the strain-rate dependency of the yield strength under dynamic conditions would be much higher than that under quasi-static conditions. However, the mechanism of the special phenomenon for the high-entropy alloy deformed at high strain rates (beyond 1 × 103 s−1) is not clear yet. Serration characteristics are ubiquitous in many structural and functional materials such as high-entropy alloy (AlCoCr1.5Fe1.5NiTi0.5, Al0.3CoCrFeNi etc.). It would lead to the instability of mechanical properties. By studying the serration behavior, it may be possible to have an early warning signal for oncoming epileptic seizures and perhaps economic trends. In the present work, we used the split-Hopkinson pressure bar to investigate the dynamic mechanical behavior of NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy prepared by arc melting. The aims are: (1) To report the mechanical properties and microstructure under dynamic loadings, (2) to obtain the plastic model, and (3) to discuss the microstructural mechanism for the serration behavior when the alloy deforms at high strain rates.
